agent_summary:
Target is OWASP Juice Shop (Angular SPA + Node/Express behind nginx), reachable only over http://juice.lab.test (https refused). Recon was empty so I mapped the surface from main.js and the REST/API endpoints (~60 read-only requests).

DONE items:
- INPV-05 SQL injection: CONFIRMED critical. /rest/products/search?q=') returns a raw SQLite syntax error; UNION payload dumped the Users table (emails + MD5 password hashes). The Sequelize id route /api/Products/1' safely 404s, so only the search q param is injectable. (Lead: critical)
- INPV-01 Reflected XSS: tested — search reflects into JSON and escapes payloads; track-order id is sanitised (quote stripped). No server-side reflected XSS found; known Juice Shop XSS are DOM/stored client-side.
- INPV-03 Verb tampering: GET and HEAD on /api/Users both 401; OPTIONS advertises all methods but auth is enforced per method — no bypass.
- INPV-04 HPP: duplicate q params change the query result (array parsing) but no bypass achieved.

N/A (feature absent): INPV-06 LDAP, INPV-08 SSI, INPV-09 XPath, INPV-10 IMAP/SMTP, INPV-13 format string, INPV-16 incoming-request/proxy monitoring.

OPEN (require writes/auth or transport control not available in this read-only lane): INPV-02 stored XSS (feedback comments store raw unencoded HTML — sink documented), INPV-07 XML/XXE (B2B order endpoint exists, OPTIONS 204), INPV-11 code injection (web3 sandbox/coding challenges are POST), INPV-12 command injection (no read-only sink), INPV-14 incubated (depends on stored sink), INPV-15 HTTP splitting/smuggling (gateway controls request line/headers), INPV-17 host header injection (Host gateway-controlled; X-Forwarded-Host not reflected on static index), INPV-18 SSTI (/profile and /dataerasure are Pug pages but need authenticated field writes; anti-tamper guard observed), INPV-19 SSRF (profile-image-by-URL is a POST).

Additional leads recorded for other lanes/reviewer: poison-null-byte bypass of the /ftp file-type allowlist (/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md serves the backup containing a JWT secret, 403 without it) — HIGH; unauthenticated user data (password hashes, totpSecret, deluxeToken) via /rest/memories — HIGH; open redirect via allowlist bypass in /redirect?to= — MEDIUM; /ftp directory listing of sensitive files — MEDIUM; public /metrics — LOW; verbose Express stack traces leaking file paths — LOW.

leads.title: [agent] Critical UNION-based SQL injection in /rest/products/search (q parameter) dumps Users table

detail.text: GET /rest/products/search?q=') returns a 500 SQLite syntax error, confirming unsanitised string concatenation. The payload q=qwert')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,'4','5','6','7','8','9' FROM Users-- returns 200 and renders every Users row as a product, exposing user emails and MD5 password hashes (e.g. admin hash 0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500). Unauthenticated, read-only reproduction.

leads.title: [agent] Directory listing of /ftp exposes sensitive files

detail.text: GET /ftp returns a browsable directory listing with 11 entries including incident-support.kdbx (KeePass DB), package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak, announcement_encrypted.md and encrypt.pyc. Static files are served and listed without authentication; several are backup/credential files.

leads.title: [agent] Feedback comments store and return raw HTML (stored XSS sink)

detail.text:
GET /api/Feedbacks returns comments containing unescaped HTML, e.g. id 6 "This is the store..." and id 5 with "
Support Team...". The comment field is persisted and served without encoding; the Angular frontend renders these, indicating a stored-XSS sink. Confirming injection would require submitting feedback (POST), which is out of scope for this read-only lane.

leads.title: [agent] Open redirect via allowlist bypass in /redirect?to=

detail.text: GET /redirect?to=https://evil.attacker.test/x?url=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returns 302 with Location: https://evil.attacker.test/x?url=... The allowlist only checks whether a whitelisted URL string appears anywhere in the target, so appending it as a query param bypasses the check and redirects to an attacker domain.

leads.title: [agent] Poison null byte bypasses /ftp file-type allowlist (backup file disclosure)

detail.text: Direct GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns 403 and /ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak would be blocked, but appending an encoded null byte and allowed extension (GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md and /ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak%2500.md) returns 200 with the raw file (application/octet-stream). The null byte truncates the server-side extension check. package.json.bak content triggered redaction of a jsonwebtoken secret and an email, indicating sensitive data disclosure. This is a null-byte input-validation / path-traversal flaw.

GET /metrics returns full Prometheus metrics (process CPU/memory, event loop lag, http_requests_count by status, startup task durations, LLM token counters). No auth required; discloses internal operational telemetry.

GET /rest/memories (no auth) returns photo-wall entries with the full embedded User object for each: username, email, password hash, role (incl. admin bkimminich), deluxeToken, lastLoginIp, totpSecret. Sensitive account data is disclosed to anonymous users.

leads.title: [agent] Verbose Express stack traces leak server file paths on errors

detail.text: Error responses (e.g. GET /rest/track-order/<encoded> returns 500, GET /redirect?to=bad returns 406) include full Node/Express stack traces with absolute paths like /juice-shop/build/routes/redirect.js and /juice-shop/node_modules/express/... This improper error handling discloses internal paths and framework versions (Express ^4.22.1).

evidence.summary: [agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/products/search?q=') -> 500. GET /rest/products/search?q=') returned a 500 with raw SQLite error "near ')': syntax error", proving the q parameter is concatenated into SQL. A UNION payload (q=qwert')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,... FROM Users--) returned HTTP 200 with the Users table dumped into product rows (emails and MD5 password hashes in the name/description fields), confirming exploitable UNION-based SQLi.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/products/search?q=apple -> 200. Single q=apple on /rest/products/search returned 3 matching products; sending duplicate parameters q=apple&q=orange returned {"data":[]} (empty). The differing result shows Express parses duplicated query params into an array, changing the query behaviour (HTTP parameter pollution handling), though no security bypass was achieved.

Full host-header injection (e.g. password-reset link poisoning) could not be exercised read-only.

items.na_reason: [agent] Juice Shop uses SQLite (relational) and MongoDB for data and does not authenticate or query against any LDAP directory; there is no LDAP-backed functionality to inject into.
[agent] The app is an Angular SPA served by nginx with a Node/Express API; there is no Server-Side Includes engine or .shtml processing in the request path, so SSI injection is not applicable.
[agent] No XML/XPath-backed query functionality exists; data access is via Sequelize (SQLite) and MongoDB. There is no XPath query to inject into.
[agent] No reachable IMAP/SMTP-interacting endpoint takes user-controlled mail headers in a read-only path; the app has no mail-proxy functionality exposed to anonymous GET requests.
[agent] Backend is Node.js/Express; user input is not passed to C-style format-string functions. No format-string sink is present in the reachable endpoints.
